case.name: bottom-mounted vertical circular cylinder, linear wave diffraction, deep water
case.physical_background: A vertical circular pile in deep water scatters an incident Airy wave; the total horizontal force per unit length follows from the Hankel-function solution of the 2-D Helmholtz diffraction problem. The closed form is the classical diffraction reference used to grade a 3-D panel solver at zero forward speed.

conditions.units_note: SI; force is per unit length of pile (2-D reduction, deep water)

primary.title: Hulme (1982) floating-hemisphere exciting force, recomputed by tensorbem.analytic.hulme_hemisphere_radiation

source.identifier_note: no external identifier: the reference is this repository's own series

reference_method.equation: F_x(ka) = 4*rho*g*A*tanh(k*h) / (k^2 * H_1^(1)'(k*a)),  k = ka/a; deep water: tanh(k*h) = 1
reference_method.derivation: re-implemented from the published closed form with scipy.special only; it does not import or call the solver being graded

uncertainty.note: the reference carries no truncation error; its physical limitations (linearised free surface, inviscid, no flow separation) are model error shared by the solver, so they cancel in this comparison

C_M = |F| / (rho g A pi a^2); approaches the Morison value 2 as ka -> 0

limit_checks.reference_locator: long-wave limit of the MacCamy & Fuchs force: C_M -> 2 (Morison inertia coefficient), Newman (1977) sec. 7.5
limit_checks.extrapolation: C_M(ka) = 2 + O(ka^2); L = (4*C_M(ka/2) - C_M(ka))/3 with ka = 0.05
limit_checks.note: graded on the tolerance only: the reference is a stated limit, so there is no pointwise closed form to reproduce at 1e-6

tolerance.policy: platform ledger: an error above 5 % is not acceptable evidence
